children: The S&P Global South Korea Manufacturing PMI fell to 51.3 in October 2026 from 53.9 in September, indicating a modest improvement in manufacturing conditions, albeit at the slowest pace since February.
Production expanded at its weakest pace so far this year as new order growth slowed, with firms citing material shortages and high costs as constraints.
New export order growth also moderated, reaching its weakest level in the current four-month sequence.
Backlogs of work rose at the slowest pace in seven months.
Meanwhile, employment decreased for the first time in four months, while purchasing activity rose more slowly.
Pre-production inventories also declined at the steepest rate since April 2020.
Regarding prices, input costs rose sharply due to higher raw material prices, although output price inflation slowed to an 11-month low.
Despite these challenges, business confidence remained robust, supported by planned product launches and sustained semiconductor demand.

title: South Korea Manufacturing Growth Slows to 8-Month Low
